chunks: Ja'far ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdullah ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to me, from his grandfather Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said:
Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Dawud (peace be upon him): 'O Dawud! Just as the sun does not diminish for one who sits in it, likewise My mercy does not diminish for one who enters into it.
And just as evil omens do not harm one who does not believe in them, likewise the superstitious ones will not be saved from tribulation.
And just as the closest of people to Me on the Day of Resurrection are the humble, likewise the furthest of people from Me on the Day of Resurrection are the arrogant.'

key_terms.الطيرة: Evil omen / superstition (tiyarah) — the pre-Islamic Arab practice of deriving omens from birds' flight, condemned in Islam
key_terms.المتكبرون: The arrogant ones (mutakabbirun) — those who practice kibr (arrogance), considered one of the greatest sins
key_terms.المتواضعون: The humble ones (mutawadi'un) — those who practice tawadu' (humility), a central Islamic virtue
key_terms.رحمتي: My mercy — refers to divine mercy (rahmah), one of God's central attributes in Islamic theology

ai.seo_question: What did Allah reveal to Prophet Dawud about divine mercy, superstition, and humility?
ai.summary: In this hadith qudsi transmitted through the Imams from the Prophet (SAWW), Allah reveals to Prophet Dawud (AS) three powerful analogies. The first compares divine mercy to sunlight — unlimited and available to all who seek it. The second warns that superstitious belief in evil omens is itself the cause of spiritual tribulation. The third establishes that humility draws one near to God while arrogance creates distance. These were teachings the Prophet shared with his community to illustrate God's boundless mercy, the foolishness of superstition, and the supreme importance of humility.
